title: Rava son of Rav Idi bar Avin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Shabbat 136a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.136a.16), Rav Papa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua came to the house of Rava [[so it is in the Rosh](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_on_Shabbat.19.7)], son of Rav Idi bar Avin. He prepared for them a third-born calf on its seventh day and they said to him: “Had you waited for it until evening, we would have eaten of it.”
In the Gemara it reads only “the son of Rav Idi bar Avin.”

notes.text: The calf was on its seventh day, rather than the incident being seven days after a son’s birth. Saved Davidson Shabbat 136a calls it third-born and has the guests say to their host that waiting would have let them eat it. The speaker direction and “third-born” wording are corrected accordingly; Rashi’s saved short wording is not claimed to supply that whole explanation.

The linked Bavli leaves the host unnamed beyond his patronymic. The linked Rosh explicitly names Rava and shortens the second guest’s name to Rav Huna. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3164&lang=en) heads the notice Rabbah and reports the Rosh’s Rava reading.
